title: Dolby Vision and HDR labels and the decisions that follow from them
description: Report VideoRange and VideoRangeType as Jellyfin 12.4 does (DOVI for P5, DOVIWithEL for P7, DOVIWithHDR10, DOVIWithHLG and DOVIWithSDR for P8 by base-layer compatibility, HDR10Plus and the DOVI-with-HDR10+ variants), stop stripping them from client DTOs, and use them in the playback decision: a client whose profile allows HDR10 (or HLG, or SDR) but not Dolby Vision plays a DV file whose base layer it supports, instead of a re-encode.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed against a real Jellyfin 12.4 first (synthetic DV fixtures in a disposable jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 container): item DTOs, PlaybackInfo decisions and the master playlist's codec tag for P5, P7 and P8.1; capture in compat/captures
The scan records the DV profile, base-layer compatibility id and HDR10+ presence
Item and PlaybackInfo DTOs carry VideoRange and VideoRangeType for SDR, HDR10, HDR10Plus, HLG and each DV variant

A profile that allows HDR10 but no DOVI type direct plays or copies a P8.1 file as HDR10; one that allows nothing HDR re-encodes with tone mapping as today; P5 (no compatible base layer) is never sent to a client without DV
The decision table tests cover every VideoRangeType against jellyfin-web's own profile conditions
Checked on the dogfood with a P8.1 film and a P7 film in jellyfin-web and one TV client
source: work queue 4; internal/library/scan.go strips them today
notes: Found while preparing the task (2026-11-07): Jellyfin's labels drive decisions, not only display. jellyfin-web sends CodecProfiles conditions on VideoRangeType, and Jellyfin copies a DOVIWithHDR10 stream to an HDR10-only client (tagging it db1p in the master playlist). jellyscale reports every DV file as plain DOVI, so those films are re-encoded in software today. Built 2026-11-08: Jellyfin 12.4 labels P8 compat 0 as DOVIInvalid and compat 3 as plain HDR10, and copies a DV file whose base layer the client plays as a transcode with VideoRangeTypeNotSupported (video copied, base layer in CODECS/VIDEO-RANGE, DV brand in SUPPLEMENTAL-CODECS) rather than direct play. The fixtures carry only the dvcC box (no RPUs). The lead checks real P8.1 and P7 films in jellyfin-web on the dogfood after merge; TV clients wait for the client pivot (JS-070, JS-065). Backlog: a row scanned before this change is not tone mapped until the next scan re-probes it; a failed HDR10+ frame read leaves HDR10 until the file changes; no test copies a DV file through jellyscale's own ffmpeg path (Jellyfin's argument set drops dvcC from the init segment, checked by hand); an old api replica refuses the HEVC copy a new one offers during a rollout.
